name: Harriet Chapman
life: “I still remember trying to lift someone who told me to stop.” On Sunday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Harriet usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I want my mother at home but can't lift her. I canceled the welcome lunch until she can tell me what she needs.
appearance: Harriet has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Harriet touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Harriet tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Harriet will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To prepare a welcome the mother can physically enjoy.
family: Willa Bishop is Harriet’s older relative by marriage. Harriet leaves the first voice message. Willa calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The last home visit*, Willa says, “I knitted her a retirement scarf with a loose end deliberately sticking out.”
connections: Joel Garza (parent). They plan the welcome around the mother's feet and the adult child's strength.

reactions.situation: A relative offers to carry the patient up the stairs
reactions.response: Harriet asks the patient whether being carried is an offer they want to take up.

reactions.response: Harriet asks the filmer to lower the phone and gets another familiar face to stand by the person crying.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Harriet repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
